title.zh: 卷141 志一百十六 兵十二 马政
title.raw: 卷141 志一百十六 兵十二 马政

sentences.zh: 志一百十六

translations.literal: Treatise 116
translations.idiomatic: Treatise 116

sentences.zh: 兵十二

translations.literal: Military 12
translations.idiomatic: Military 12

sentences.zh: 馬政

translations.literal: Horse Administration
translations.idiomatic: Horse Administration

sentences.zh: 清初沿明制，設御馬監，康熙間，改為上駟院，掌御馬，以備上乘。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Qing, following the Ming system, they established the Imperial Horse Directorate; during the Kangxi period it was changed to the Superior Stud Institute, which managed imperial horses to supply mounts for riding.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Qing, the court retained the Ming arrangement and set up the Imperial Horse Directorate; under Kangxi this became the Superior Stud Institute, charged with imperial horses for the emperor's mount.

sentences.zh: 畜以備御者，曰內馬；

translations.literal: Those raised to supply imperial riding were called inner horses;
translations.idiomatic: Horses kept for the emperor's own riding were termed inner horses;

sentences.zh: 供儀仗者，曰仗馬。

translations.literal: those supplied for ceremonial regalia were called escort horses.
translations.idiomatic: those furnished for ceremonial escorts were called escort horses.

sentences.zh: 御馬選入，以印烙之。

translations.literal: When imperial horses were selected and entered, they were branded with an official seal.
translations.idiomatic: Selected imperial horses were admitted and marked with an official brand.

sentences.zh: 設蒙古馬醫官療馬病。

translations.literal: Mongol horse doctors were appointed to treat equine illness.
translations.idiomatic: Mongol equine physicians were appointed to treat sick horses.

sentences.zh: 上巡幸及行圍，扈從官弁，各給官馬。

translations.literal: When the sovereign toured or went on the hunt, each accompanying officer was given a government horse.
translations.idiomatic: On imperial tours and hunting expeditions, every officer in the entourage received a government mount.

sentences.zh: 以副都統或侍衛為放馬大臣，主其事。

translations.literal: A vice commander-in-chief or an imperial bodyguard served as commissioner for issuing horses and directed the affair.
translations.idiomatic: A vice banner commander or palace guardsman served as commissioner for issuing horses and oversaw the arrangements.

sentences.zh: 上謁祖陵，需馬二萬三千餘匹，東西陵需馬四千三百餘匹，悉取察哈爾牧廠馬應之。

translations.literal: When the sovereign visited the ancestral tombs, more than 23,000 horses were needed; for the Eastern and Western Tombs more than 4,300—all taken from Chahar pasture farms to meet the demand.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial visits to the ancestral tombs required upwards of 23,000 horses; the Eastern and Western Tombs needed more than 4,300—all drawn from Chahar pasture establishments.

sentences.zh: 迨乾隆時，每扈從用馬匹輒二萬餘。

translations.literal: By the Qianlong period, each imperial entourage routinely used more than twenty thousand horses.
translations.idiomatic: Under Qianlong, a single imperial tour commonly consumed over twenty thousand mounts.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶中，物力漸耗，停木蘭秋獮。

translations.literal: During the Jiaqing reign, material resources gradually dwindled and the autumn hunt at Mulan was suspended.
translations.idiomatic: In the Jiaqing era, resources wore thin and the autumn hunt at Mulan was discontinued.

sentences.zh: 十二年，減額馬之半。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, the allotted horses were reduced by half.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year, the official horse quota was cut in half.

sentences.zh: 道光九年，如盛京謁陵，額馬視乾隆時，約略相等，計取給廠馬暨各盟長所進，蓋二萬六千餘匹雲。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Daoguang, when visiting the tombs at Mukden, the allotted horses were roughly equal to those in Qianlong times; counting pasture horses and those presented by league chiefs, there were somewhat more than twenty-six thousand in all.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 9, the Mukden tomb visit called for a quota nearly matching Qianlong levels; between pasture stock and presentations from league chiefs, the total ran to somewhat more than twenty-six thousand horses.

sentences.zh: 順治十五年定軍馬，親王出征，馬四百匹，郡王三百，貝勒二百，貝子百五十，鎮國公百匹，輔國公八十，不入八分鎮國公七十，輔國公六十五，將軍八十，副將軍七十，護軍統領、前鋒統領、副都統皆六十，其下各有差，最少者護軍、領催各六匹。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Shunzhi military horses were fixed: a prince of the first rank on campaign, 400 horses; a prince of the second rank, 300; a beile, 200; a beise, 150; a prince of the state supporting the realm, 100; a prince assisting the realm, 80; a prince of the state supporting the realm not in the eight privileges, 70; a prince assisting the realm, 65; a general, 80; a lieutenant general, 70; commanders of the guards, vanguard, and vice banner commanders each 60; below these each had its difference, the minimum being six each for guardsmen and squad leaders.
translations.idiomatic: Shunzhi 15 codified campaign horse allotments: a first-rank prince received 400, a second-rank prince 300, a beile 200, a beise 150, a state-supporting duke 100, an assisting duke 80, a state-supporting duke outside the eight privileges 70, an assisting duke 65, a general 80, a lieutenant general 70, and commanders of the guards, vanguard, and vice banner commanders 60 each, with graded reductions below—down to six horses apiece for guardsmen and squad leaders.

sentences.zh: 康熙三十五年，敕出徵兵一人馬四匹，四人為伍，一伍主從騎八匹，馱器糧用具亦八匹。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fifth year of Kangxi, an edict fixed that each soldier on campaign had four horses; four men formed a squad; one squad had eight horses for master and followers to ride, and eight more to carry gear, grain, and utensils.
translations.idiomatic: Kangxi 35 decreed four horses per campaigning soldier; four men formed a squad, with eight mounts for riders and eight more for equipment, grain, and baggage.

sentences.zh: 是歲，征噶爾丹，以兵丁馬瘦，褫兵部尚書索諾和職。

translations.literal: That year, campaigning against Galdan, because the soldiers' horses were thin, the Minister of War Suohe was stripped of his post.
translations.idiomatic: That year, during the Galdan campaign, emaciated troop horses cost War Minister Suohe his office.

sentences.zh: 五十一年，覈定軍中職官馬數，大學士、尚書、左都御史十六匹，侍郎以下遞減，經略、大將軍各二十五匹，副將軍以下遞減。

translations.literal: In the fifty-first year, the number of horses for military offices was verified: grand secretaries, ministers, and the left censor-in-chief, sixteen each; vice-ministers and below in descending order; commissioners and grand generals, twenty-five each; lieutenant generals and below in descending order.
translations.idiomatic: In year 51, military horse quotas for officials were audited: grand secretaries, ministers, and the left censor-in-chief received sixteen each, with stepwise reductions for vice-ministers and below; commissioners and grand generals twenty-five each, and lieutenant generals and lower ranks scaled down from there.

sentences.zh: 乾隆十六年，八旗牧官馬二萬七千七百餘匹，以萬匹於都城外牧養，熱河千匹，各庄頭二千匹，餘者分畀直隸標營。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year of Qianlong, the Eight Banners pastured 27,700-odd government horses: ten thousand pastured outside the capital, a thousand at Rehe, two thousand with estate heads, the remainder distributed to Zhili garrison units.
translations.idiomatic: Qianlong 16 counted 27,700-odd banner government horses: ten thousand grazed outside the capital, one thousand at Rehe, two thousand with estate managers, and the rest allotted to Zhili garrison battalions.

sentences.zh: 圈馬之設，始乾隆二十八年，從都統舒赫德請也。

translations.literal: The establishment of corral horses began in the twenty-eighth year of Qianlong, following the request of banner commander Shuhede.
translations.idiomatic: Corralled banner horses date from Qianlong 28, at the urging of banner commander Shuhede.

sentences.zh: 滿洲八旗，旗養馬二百匹。

translations.literal: For the Manchu Eight Banners, each banner pastured 200 horses.
translations.idiomatic: Each Manchu banner maintained 200 corral horses.

sentences.zh: 蒙古八旗，旗百匹。

translations.literal: For the Mongol Eight Banners, each banner, 100.
translations.idiomatic: Each Mongol banner kept 100.

sentences.zh: 洎五十九年撤圈，分給各兵拴養。

translations.literal: By the fifty-ninth year the corrals were abolished and the horses distributed for soldiers to tether and keep.
translations.idiomatic: By year 59 the corrals were dismantled and horses assigned for individual soldier tethering.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶十二年，諭成親王永星議復圈馬，大學士戴衢亨等會議，立章程十條，圈馬仍舊。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Jiaqing, an edict ordered Prince Yongxing to deliberate on restoring corral horses; Grand Secretary Dai Yuheng and others met in council and drew up ten articles of regulation, and corral horses continued as before.
translations.idiomatic: Jiaqing 12 directed Prince Yongxing to study reviving corral horses; Grand Secretary Dai Yuheng and colleagues drafted ten regulations, and the corral system was left in place.

sentences.zh: 道光末，軍興遂廢，後亦不復籌矣。

translations.literal: At the end of Daoguang, with warfare underway it was abandoned and never revived.
translations.idiomatic: By late Daoguang, wartime needs ended the practice, and it was never restored.

sentences.zh: 同治元年諭曰：「馬政廢弛，積弊已深，以致軍馬罷瘠。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tongzhi an edict said: "Horse administration has fallen into neglect; abuses have deepened, so that military horses are worn and weak.
translations.idiomatic: Tongzhi 1 warned that horse administration had lapsed and abuses deepened until army mounts grew feeble.

sentences.zh: 牧廠大臣等應妥實整頓，差功罪以挽頹風，著為令。

translations.literal: Pasture commissioners and the like should earnestly put matters in order, distinguishing merit and fault to reverse the decline, and make this a standing rule."
translations.idiomatic: Pasture officials were to restore order, reward and punish by merit, and codify the reform as permanent law."

sentences.zh: 」溯自世祖入關，迄於康、乾之際，盛京、吉林、黑龍江、直隸、江南、浙江、廣東、福建、湖北、四川、陝、甘、山東、山西諸省設駐防滿洲營，馬凡十萬六千四百餘匹，惟福建水師駐防僅數十匹。

translations.literal: Tracing from the ancestral founder's entry into China down to the Kangxi and Qianlong era, in Shengjing, Jilin, Heilongjiang, Zhili, Jiangnan, Zhejiang, Guangdong, Fujian, Hubei, Sichuan, Shaanxi, Gansu, Shandong, and Shanxi the garrison Manchu camps were allotted 106,400-odd horses in all, only the Fujian naval garrison having a few dozen.
translations.idiomatic: From the founding entry through the Kangxi–Qianlong height, garrison Manchu forces across Shengjing, Jilin, Heilongjiang, Zhili, Jiangnan, Zhejiang, Guangdong, Fujian, Hubei, Sichuan, Shaanxi, Gansu, Shandong, and Shanxi held over 106,400 horses—Fujian's naval garrison alone kept only a few dozen.

sentences.zh: 乾隆季年，定西藏兵制，前藏供差營馬六十匹，後藏二十匹，舊塘四十三，共塘馬二百二十匹，新設番塘二十四，共番馬九十八匹。

translations.literal: In the late Qianlong years Tibet's military establishment was fixed: front Tibet, 60 horses for service duty; rear Tibet, 20; old courier stations, 43, totaling 220 courier horses; newly established Tibetan courier stations, 24, totaling 98 Tibetan horses.
translations.idiomatic: Late Qianlong fixed Tibet's horse establishment: sixty for front-Tibet service, twenty for rear Tibet, 220 across forty-three old courier posts, and ninety-eight across twenty-four new Tibetan courier posts.

sentences.zh: 黑龍江兵向無額馬，道光十六年，從哈豐阿請，始設置之。

translations.literal: Heilongjiang troops had never had allotted horses; in the sixteenth year of Daoguang, following Ha Feng'a's request, they were first established.
translations.idiomatic: Heilongjiang troops long lacked quota horses; Daoguang 16, on Ha Feng'a's petition, first assigned them.

sentences.zh: 天聰時，征服察哈爾，其地宜牧，馬蕃息。

translations.literal: In the Tiancong era, Chahar was conquered; the land was suited to pasture and horses multiplied.
translations.idiomatic: Under Tiancong, Chahar was subdued; its pasturelands thrived and herds multiplied.

sentences.zh: 順治初，大庫口外設種馬廠，隸兵部。

translations.literal: Early in Shunzhi, outside Daku Pass a stud farm was set up, subordinate to the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: Early Shunzhi saw a stud farm beyond Daku Pass, under the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 康熙九年，改牧廠屬太僕寺，分左翼右翼二廠，均在口外。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Kangxi, pasture farms were transferred to the Court of the Imperial Stud, divided into left and right wings, both outside the pass.
translations.idiomatic: Kangxi 9 placed pasture farms under the Court of the Imperial Stud as separate left- and right-wing establishments beyond the pass.

sentences.zh: 是時，大凌河設牧廠一，邊牆設廠二，曰商都達布遜諾爾，曰達里岡愛，隸上駟院。

translations.literal: At that time one pasture farm was set at Dalinhe, and two along the border wall, called Shangdu Dabuxun Lake and Daligangai, subordinate to the Superior Stud Institute.
translations.idiomatic: Then one farm stood at Dalinhe and two along the border wall—Shangdu Dabuxun Lake and Daligangai—under the Superior Stud Institute.

sentences.zh: 尋分設牧廠五，曰大凌河牧群馬營，曰養息牧哈達牧群馬營，曰養息所邊外蘇魯克牧牛羊群，及黑牛群牧營，曰養息牧邊外牧群牛營，並在盛京境。

translations.literal: Soon five pasture farms were separately established: the Dalinhe Pasture Horse Camp; the Yangxi Pasture Hada Pasture Horse Camp; the Yangxi Pasture Beyond-the-Pass Suluoke Pasture Cattle and Sheep Herd, and Black Cattle Herd Camp; the Yangxi Pasture Beyond-the-Pass Pasture Cattle Camp—all within Shengjing territory.
translations.idiomatic: Five farms followed: Dalinhe Pasture Horse Camp; Yangxi Hada Pasture Horse Camp; Yangxi beyond-the-pass Suluoke cattle-and-sheep herd and black-cattle camp; and Yangxi beyond-the-pass pasture cattle camp—all in Shengjing.

sentences.zh: 凡馬牡曰兒，牝曰果，不及三歲曰駒，及壯擇割其牡曰騸。

translations.literal: For horses, the male was called er, the female guo; those under three years, colts; when mature the male was selected and castrated, called shan.
translations.idiomatic: Stallions were termed er, mares guo, foals under three years ju; mature males selected for castration were called shan.

sentences.zh: 別其騍騸以為群，率騍馬五配兒馬一，群無過四百匹。

translations.literal: Stallions and geldings were separated into herds; generally five stallions to one er; no herd exceeded 400 head.
translations.idiomatic: Stallions and geldings formed separate herds at roughly five stallions per breeding male, capped at four hundred head per herd.

sentences.zh: 騍馬及羊三年一平群，牛六年，騍馬群三歲以息補耗，三馬而取一駒，騸馬群歲耗其十一。

translations.literal: Stallion herds and sheep were balanced every three years, cattle every six; stallion herds replenished losses at three years; three horses yielded one colt; gelding herds lost one in eleven yearly.
translations.idiomatic: Stallion herds and sheep were tallied every three years, cattle every six; stallion herds replaced attrition triennially at one colt per three mares; gelding herds wrote off one eleventh annually.

sentences.zh: 置牧長、牧副、牧丁任其事，轄以協領、翼長、總管，官兵皆察哈爾、蒙古人充之。

translations.literal: Pasture chiefs, assistants, and hands were appointed for the work, under assistant commandants, wing chiefs, and superintendents; officers and men were all Chahar and Mongols.
translations.idiomatic: Pasture chiefs, deputies, and hands ran operations under assistant commandants, wing chiefs, and superintendents, staffed entirely by Chahar and Mongol personnel.

sentences.zh: 飼秣所需木槽鏇钁鑹杓，每群各二，五年一給之。

translations.literal: Wooden troughs, augers, hoes, spades, and ladles needed for fodder—two of each per herd, issued every five years.
translations.idiomatic: Fodder gear—wooden troughs, augers, hoes, spades, and ladles—came two sets per herd on a five-year issue cycle.

sentences.zh: 總管三年番代。

translations.literal: Superintendents rotated every three years.
translations.idiomatic: Superintendents served three-year rotations.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，定牧群牲畜歲終彙報增減數目，視其贏絀，以第賞罰。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year, at year-end pasture herds reported increases and decreases; according to surplus or deficit, rewards and punishments were ranked.
translations.idiomatic: Year 24 required year-end herd reports of gains and losses, with graded rewards or penalties for surplus or shortfall.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，令八旗豢馬，春夏驅赴察哈爾牧放，曰出青，秋冬迴圈，曰回青。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year, an order fixed that Eight Banner horse-keeping: spring and summer drove them to Chahar pasture, called going out to green; autumn and winter returned to the corral, called returning to green.
translations.idiomatic: Year 26 ordered banner horses out to Chahar pastures spring and summer ("going out to green") and back to corrals autumn and winter ("returning to green").

sentences.zh: 四十四年，將軍楊福請市馬給兵丁，上不許，諭曰：「朝廷屢以太僕寺廠馬並茶馬給各兵丁，故無賠馬之苦。

translations.literal: In the forty-fourth year, General Yang Fu requested purchasing horses for soldiers; the emperor did not permit it and instructed: "The court has repeatedly given Court of the Imperial Stud pasture horses and tea horses to each soldier, so there is no hardship of compensating horses.
translations.idiomatic: Year 44, General Yang Fu sought market purchases for troops; the emperor refused, noting repeated allotments of stud-farm and tea-trade horses that spared soldiers compensation burdens.

sentences.zh: 歷觀宋、明議馬政，皆無善策。

translations.literal: Looking through Song and Ming discussions of horse policy, none had good measures.
translations.idiomatic: "Song and Ming horse-policy debates," he observed, "never produced a sound plan."

sentences.zh: 牧馬惟口外最善，水草肥美，不糜餉而孳生甚多。

translations.literal: Pasturing horses only beyond the pass was best—water and grass lush and fat, multiplying greatly without consuming rations.
translations.idiomatic: Only beyond-the-pass grazing excelled—rich forage multiplying herds without draining provisions.

sentences.zh: 如驅入內地牧之，即日費萬金不足矣。

translations.literal: If driven to pasture within the interior, even ten thousand in gold a day would not suffice."
translations.idiomatic: Driving herds inland, he added, would cost ten thousand taels a day and still fall short."

sentences.zh: 」雍正三年，定在廠馬以四萬匹為率。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yongzheng, pasture horses were fixed at 40,000 as the standard.
translations.idiomatic: Yongzheng 3 set a 40,000-head quota for pasture horses.

sentences.zh: 至乾隆五年，足額外，溢七千餘匹。

translations.literal: By the fifth year of Qianlong, beyond filling the quota there was a surplus of more than 7,000.
translations.idiomatic: By Qianlong 5 the quota was met with 7,000-odd head to spare.

sentences.zh: 兩翼牧廠，共騍馬百六十群，騸馬十六群，令分在兩翼廠牧放。

translations.literal: The two wing pasture farms had 160 stallion herds and 16 gelding herds in all, ordered pastured separately on the two wing farms.
translations.idiomatic: Both wings together ran 160 stallion herds and 16 gelding herds, each wing grazing its allotment.

sentences.zh: 八年，敕牧界毋許侵越。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, an edict forbade encroachment on pasture boundaries.
translations.idiomatic: Year 8 forbade encroachment on pasture boundaries.

sentences.zh: 先是甘、涼、肅三州及西寧各設馬廠，分五群，群儲牝馬二百匹，牡四十。

translations.literal: Earlier Gansu, Liangzhou, Suzhou, and Xining each had horse farms, divided into five herds; each herd kept 200 brood mares and 40 stallions.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Gansu, Liangzhou, Suzhou, and Xining each maintained horse farms in five herds of 200 brood mares and 40 stallions.

sentences.zh: 尋改甘州廠屬巴里坤。

translations.literal: Soon the Ganzhou farm was transferred to Barkul.
translations.idiomatic: The Ganzhou farm was soon reassigned to Barkul.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，伊犁設孳生馬駝廠，畀錫伯、察哈爾、索倫、厄魯特四營牧之。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year, Ili established breeding horse and camel farms, assigned to Xibe, Chahar, Solon, and Olot camps for pasturing.
translations.idiomatic: Year 25 founded Ili breeding farms for horses and camels, pastured by Xibe, Chahar, Solon, and Olot detachments.

sentences.zh: 三十二年，定牧廠官屬所需馬，視內地驛傳例，按官品給之，不得逾額。

translations.literal: In the thirty-second year, horses needed by pasture officials were fixed like the interior relay-post precedent, given by official rank and not to exceed the quota.
translations.idiomatic: Year 32 capped officials' personal mounts by rank on the interior relay-post model.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶中，從都統慶溥言，撤回厄魯特人牧廠。

translations.literal: During Jiaqing, following banner commander Qing Pu's statement, Olot pasture herds were withdrawn.
translations.idiomatic: Jiaqing, on banner commander Qing Pu's advice, withdrew Olot pasture detachments.

sentences.zh: 初，富俊建言，撤大凌河牧廠，分歸東三省，仁宗嚴諭斥之。

translations.literal: Initially Fu Jun proposed abolishing the Dalinhe pasture farm and distributing it to the three eastern provinces; the Renzong Emperor sternly rebuked this.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jun had urged abolishing Dalinhe and redistributing stock to the northeast; the Jiaqing Emperor sharply rejected it.

sentences.zh: 迨道光七年，上經杏山東閱馬廠，見河岸馬群壯整。

translations.literal: By the seventh year of Daoguang, the emperor passed Xingshan east inspecting horse farms and saw herds along the riverbank strong and orderly.
translations.idiomatic: Daoguang 7 brought the emperor east of Xingshan to inspect farms and find riverbank herds sturdy and well-formed.

sentences.zh: 因諭是間牧廠寬闊，水草蕃滋，馬恃以生息，若輕議裁，則散之甚易，聚之甚難。

translations.literal: He therefore instructed that the pasture farms here were broad, water and grass abundant, and horses relied on them to multiply; if lightly proposed for reduction, dispersing would be very easy but gathering very hard.
translations.idiomatic: He noted the wide pastures and rich forage sustaining the herds, warning that careless cuts would scatter stock easily yet reunite them only with great difficulty.

sentences.zh: 再有率為此請者，以違制論。

translations.literal: Whoever again led such a proposal was to be punished for violating regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Further proposals of that kind would be punished as regulatory violations.

sentences.zh: 咸豐四年，科爾沁親王僧格林沁剿捻，檄取察哈爾戰馬六百匹，不堪乘用，奏聞。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Xianfeng, Prince Sengge Rinchen of Khorchin suppressed the Nian rebels and requisitioned 600 Chahar war horses, unfit for riding; this was reported.
translations.idiomatic: Xianfeng 4, Khorchin Prince Sengge Rinchen's Nian campaign requisitioned 600 Chahar war horses, reported unfit to ride.

sentences.zh: 上大怒，嚴諭都統慶昀整頓，蓋馬政漸衰弛矣。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly angered and sternly ordered banner commander Qing Yun to put matters in order—horse administration was gradually declining.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's wrath fell on banner commander Qing Yun to restore order—horse administration was plainly slipping.

sentences.zh: 光緒九年，太僕寺言兩翼騍馬騸馬一百十四群，並孳生馬五群，駝亦五群，較乾隆時群數大減。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Guangxu, the Court of the Imperial Stud reported that the two wings' stallion and gelding herds totaled 114 herds, plus five breeding horse herds and five camel herds—a great reduction from Qianlong numbers.
translations.idiomatic: Guangxu 9 reported the two wings down to 114 stallion and gelding herds, five breeding-horse herds, and five camel herds—far below Qianlong levels.

sentences.zh: 嗣是穆圖善練兵，至黑龍江求馬無良，愀然曰：「地氣其盡乎！

translations.literal: Thereafter Mutushan drilled troops; reaching Heilongjiang he sought horses and found none sound, and said mournfully: "Has the land's vital force been exhausted!"
translations.idiomatic: Later Mutushan trained troops; in Heilongjiang he found no sound horses and mourned, "Has the land's breath run out!"

sentences.zh: 」迨於末葉，厲行新法，舊時牧政益廢不講，豈非時勢使然歟？

translations.literal: By the final years, vigorously enacting new methods, the old pasture administration was increasingly abandoned and not discussed—is this not what the times compelled?
translations.idiomatic: In the dynasty's last years, new reforms left old pasture policy in disuse—perhaps inevitability of the age?

sentences.zh: 順治初，陝西設洮岷、河州、西寧、庄浪、甘州茶馬司，及開成、安定、廣寧、黑水、清平、萬安、武安七監，歲遣御史一人專理之。

translations.literal: Early in Shunzhi, Shaanxi established the Taomin, Hezhou, Xining, Zhuanglang, and Ganzhou tea-horse offices, and seven stud offices—Kaicheng, Anding, Guangning, Heishui, Qingping, Wan'an, and Wu'an—each year dispatching one censor to manage them exclusively.
translations.idiomatic: Early Shunzhi Shaanxi set up Taomin, Hezhou, Xining, Zhuanglang, and Ganzhou tea-horse offices plus seven studs—Kaicheng, Anding, Guangning, Heishui, Qingping, Wan'an, and Wu'an—overseen annually by a dedicated censor.

sentences.zh: 七年，喀爾喀、額魯特來市馬，諭令自章京監察之販客及賈人，與不系披甲者，概不許購，違者鞭一百，馬入官。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, Khalkha and Elut came to market horses; an edict ordered that from supervising clerks and brokers down to traders and persons not in armor, none might purchase; violators received 100 lashes and horses entered government stock.
translations.idiomatic: Year 7, when Khalkha and Elut brought horses to market, clerks, brokers, merchants, and unarmed men were forbidden to buy; violators took 100 lashes and forfeited the animals.

sentences.zh: 蒙古攜馬來京，不許商販私買，胥役私購者罪之。

translations.literal: Mongols bringing horses to the capital were not permitted private purchase by merchants; clerks who privately bought were punished.
translations.idiomatic: Mongol horses brought to the capital could not be bought privately; clerks who did were punished.

sentences.zh: 康熙七年，裁茶馬御史，以馬政歸甘肅巡撫。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Kangxi the tea-horse censor was abolished and horse affairs returned to the Gansu governor.
translations.idiomatic: Kangxi 7 abolished the tea-horse censor and placed horse affairs under the Gansu governor.

sentences.zh: 三十四年，諭遣師中等往蒙古諸旗購馬，歸化城、科爾沁各二千匹，餘定額有差。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fourth year, an edict dispatched Shi Zhong and others to purchase horses in the Mongol banners: 2,000 each at Guihuacheng and Khorchin, the remainder in graded quotas.
translations.idiomatic: Year 34 sent Shi Zhong and others to buy horses in Mongol leagues—2,000 each at Guihuacheng and Khorchin, with graded quotas elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 乾隆十二年，禁朝鮮買馬。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Qianlong, Korea's horse purchases were forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: Qianlong 12 banned Korean horse purchases.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，敕烏魯木齊市易哈薩克馬百三十餘匹歸巴里坤。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year, an edict ordered horses bartered with Kazakhs at Urumqi—130-odd head—sent to Barkul.
translations.idiomatic: Year 25 directed 130-odd Kazakh horses traded at Urumqi to Barkul.

sentences.zh: 旋以五吉等言，選哈薩克所易馬撥往巴里坤，遂停購買。

translations.literal: Soon, on Wuji's statement, Kazakh horses from the trade were selected and sent to Barkul, and purchases were halted.
translations.idiomatic: Soon, on Wuji's advice, selected Kazakh trade horses went to Barkul and purchases stopped.

sentences.zh: 阿桂言伊犁易來哈薩克馬漸成大群，敕書嘉予。

translations.literal: Agui reported that horses from Ili's Kazakh trade were gradually forming large herds; an edict praised and rewarded this.
translations.idiomatic: Agui reported Ili's Kazakh trade horses forming large herds; the court praised and rewarded the achievement.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，定江寧、浙江、福建駐防馬匹出口採買例。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year, regulations were fixed for garrison horse purchases exported from Jiangning, Zhejiang, and Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: Year 28 regulated export purchases for Jiangning, Zhejiang, and Fujian garrison horses.

sentences.zh: 三十二年，以伊犁易哈薩克馬累積至多，擇巴里坤善地牧放。

translations.literal: In the thirty-second year, because Ili's Kazakh trade horses had accumulated to a great number, good pasture at Barkul was chosen for grazing.
translations.idiomatic: Year 32, with Ili's Kazakh trade horses accumulating, chose good Barkul pasture for grazing.

sentences.zh: 尋烏里雅蘇台馬缺，亦以哈薩克馬換易之。

translations.literal: Soon Uliastai lacked horses and also bartered Kazakh horses to fill the gap.
translations.idiomatic: When Uliastai ran short, Kazakh horses filled the gap by barter as well.

sentences.zh: 陝、甘營馬，例調自伊犁轉補，道遠耗時。

translations.literal: Shaanxi and Gansu garrison horses were routinely transferred from Ili for replenishment—a distant road consuming much time.
translations.idiomatic: Shaanxi and Gansu garrisons routinely replenished from distant Ili transfers—a slow, costly route.

sentences.zh: 咸豐四年，用賡福請，由伊犁、塔爾巴哈台隨地變價，令各營自購。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Xianfeng, following Geng Fu's request, Ili and Tarbagatai sold horses locally at adjusted prices for each camp to purchase itself.
translations.idiomatic: Xianfeng 4, on Geng Fu's petition, let Ili and Tarbagatai sell horses locally at adjusted prices for garrisons to buy on site.

sentences.zh: 七年，並敕山東缺額馬，亦就近買補雲。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, an edict also ordered Shandong's shortfall in allotted horses to be bought and filled nearby.
translations.idiomatic: Year 7 extended the same nearby-purchase rule to Shandong's quota shortfalls.

sentences.zh: 貢馬昉於國初，歸化城土默特二旗，每歲四時貢馬百匹。

translations.literal: Tribute horses began at the founding of the state: the Tumed two banners of Guihuacheng each season presented 100 horses.
translations.idiomatic: Tribute horses began at the dynasty's founding: Guihuacheng's two Tumed banners presented 100 horses each season.

sentences.zh: 順治十三年，吐魯番貢三百二十四匹，嗣減令貢西馬四匹，蒙古馬十匹。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Shunzhi, Turfan presented 324; later reduced to four Western horses and ten Mongol horses yearly.
translations.idiomatic: Shunzhi 13 brought 324 Turfan horses; later tribute fell to four Western and ten Mongol horses yearly.

sentences.zh: 康熙八年，以邊外蒙古貢馬，沿途抑買，諭嚴禁之。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Kangxi, because frontier Mongol tribute horses were suppressed and bought along the route, an edict strictly forbade this.
translations.idiomatic: Kangxi 8 forbade forced purchases of frontier Mongol tribute horses en route.

sentences.zh: 三十年，諭土謝圖、車臣俱留汗號，貢白駝一、白馬八如初，自餘毋以九白進。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year, an edict to the Tushiyetu and Tsetsen Khanates retained their titles; tribute of one white camel and eight white horses as at first—nothing more of the nine whites.
translations.idiomatic: Year 30 confirmed titles for the Tushiyetu and Tsetsen khans while limiting tribute to one white camel and eight white horses as originally—no further "nine whites."

sentences.zh: 三十五年，喀爾喀蒙古獻駝馬，多不可計，感聖祖破噶爾丹，得歸原牧地也。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fifth year, Khalkha Mongols presented camels and horses beyond counting, grateful that the sage ancestor destroyed Galdan and they could return to their original pastures.
translations.idiomatic: Year 35 brought uncountable Khalkha camel and horse tribute, offered in gratitude for Kangxi's defeat of Galdan and restoration of their pastures.

sentences.zh: 四川各土司例貢及折徵馬，各營少者一、二匹，最多十二匹。

translations.literal: Sichuan native chieftains presented tribute and commuted horses by regulation; each camp had at minimum one or two, at most twelve.
translations.idiomatic: Sichuan chieftains presented tribute and commuted horse levies by regulation—one or two per camp at minimum, twelve at most.

sentences.zh: 甘肅唐古特七族西喇古兒例貢馬匹，各營最多者八十二匹，少者遞減至二、三匹。

translations.literal: Gansu's seven Tangut Xilaogu'er tribes presented horses by precedent; each camp had at most 82, decreasing to two or three.
translations.idiomatic: Gansu's seven Tangut Xilaogu'er tribes presented by precedent—up to eighty-two horses per camp, down to two or three.

sentences.zh: 乾隆元年，諭四川土司折價馬每匹納銀十二兩，通省營馬改從驛馬例，納銀八兩，永著為令。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qianlong, an edict fixed Sichuan chieftain commuted horses at twelve taels of silver each; province-wide garrison horses followed the relay-post precedent at eight taels, permanently established.
translations.idiomatic: Qianlong 1 set Sichuan chieftain commutation at twelve taels per horse and province-wide garrison commutation at eight taels on the relay-post model, as permanent law.

sentences.zh: 三十年，哈薩克沁德穆爾等獻馬。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year, Qinde Mu'er of the Kazakhs and others presented horses.
translations.idiomatic: Year 30 brought horses from Kazakh Qinde Mu'er and others.

sentences.zh: 敕其餘馬赴伊犁，毋於喀什噶爾諸地貿易。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the remaining horses sent to Ili and not traded at Kashgar and other places.
translations.idiomatic: Surplus animals were ordered to Ili, not to Kashgar markets.

sentences.zh: 尋令沙拉伯爾游牧之哈薩克，與沙拉伯爾一體貢馬。

translations.literal: Soon Kazakhs pasturing at Shalabuer were ordered to present tribute horses together with Shalabuer as one.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Kazakhs grazing Shalabuer were grouped with Shalabuer for joint horse tribute.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶元年，停葉爾羌進馬。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jiaqing, Yarkand's horse presentations were halted.
translations.idiomatic: Jiaqing 1 ended Yarkand horse presentations.

sentences.zh: 十六年，諭烏里雅蘇台將軍等貢馬及備用馬選取之。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year, an edict to the Uliastai general and others to select from presented and reserve horses.
translations.idiomatic: Year 16 directed the Uliastai general and others to select from tribute and reserve stock.

sentences.zh: 又諭伊犁進馬，材具佶閒，足供御用，令正備貢各五匹，有私帶者，以違制論。

translations.literal: Again an edict on Ili presentations: the quality stout and fit for imperial use; fix formal tribute at five each for main and reserve; private extras punished as violations.
translations.idiomatic: Ili tribute must be stout and imperial-grade: five main and five reserve; extras treated as violations.

sentences.zh: 道光二年，從那彥成奏，青海屬玉樹番族歲納貢馬，據丁口數，依二十壯丁貢馬一匹例，按數遞裁。

translations.literal: In the second year of Daoguang, following Nayancheng's memorial, Qinghai's Yushu Tibetan tribes' yearly tribute horses, based on household count, followed the precedent of one horse per twenty adult males, reduced by graded count.
translations.idiomatic: Daoguang 2, on Nayancheng's memorial, scaled Qinghai Yushu Tibetan tribute by households on the one-horse-per-twenty-adult-male rule with graded reductions.

sentences.zh: 涼州屬番族歲仍納馬一匹。

translations.literal: Liangzhou's subordinate Tibetan tribes still presented one horse yearly.
translations.idiomatic: Liangzhou Tibetan subjects still presented one horse annually.

sentences.zh: 初內外蒙部多貴戚，每征伐，爭先輸馬、駝，漢、唐以來所未有也。

translations.literal: Initially inner and outer Mongolia had many nobles; each campaign they vied to present horses and camels first—a thing not seen since Han and Tang.
translations.idiomatic: Early on, inner and outer Mongolia's nobles raced to present horses and camels at each campaign—unmatched since Han and Tang times.

sentences.zh: 康熙初，察哈爾親王、郡王、貝勒等，聞三籓叛，各獻馬匹佐軍。

translations.literal: Early in Kangxi, Chahar princes, second-rank princes, beiles, and the like, hearing of the Three Feudatories' rebellion, each presented horses to assist the army.
translations.idiomatic: Early Kangxi, hearing of the Three Feudatories' revolt, Chahar princes and beiles each sent horses to support the armies.

sentences.zh: 道光九年，章佳胡圖克圖捐馬百匹，收其半。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Daoguang, the Zhangjia Khutuktu donated 100 horses; half were accepted.
translations.idiomatic: Daoguang 9, the Zhangjia Khutuktu donated 100 horses; the court accepted half.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，察哈爾蒙旗捐馬千九百七十匹。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year, Chahar Mongol banners donated 1,970 horses.
translations.idiomatic: In year 23, Chahar Mongol banners presented 1,970 horses.

sentences.zh: 咸豐初，哲布尊丹巴等捐馬千匹，喀爾喀土謝圖等二千匹，錫林果勒盟長等三千匹，帝以其多，卻之。

translations.literal: Early in Xianfeng, Jebzundamba and others donated 1,000 horses; Khalkha Tushiyetu and others, 2,000; league chiefs of Xilingol, 3,000; the emperor, because they were too many, declined them.
translations.idiomatic: Early Xianfeng brought 1,000 horses from Jebzundamba, 2,000 from Khalkha Tushiyetu, and 3,000 from Xilingol league chiefs; the emperor declined them as excessive.

sentences.zh: 嗣聞已在途中，令擇善地牧以待用。

translations.literal: Soon hearing they were already on the road, he ordered good pasture chosen to keep them until needed.
translations.idiomatic: Learning they were already en route, he ordered them pastured at a suitable site until required.

sentences.zh: 自是三音諾顏部等，以軍事輸馬、駝，旋捐馬二千一百，錫林果勒盟等千二百，或留或否。

translations.literal: From then the Setsen Khan and others, because of military affairs presented horses and camels, soon donated 2,100 horses; Xilingol League and others, 1,200—some retained, some not.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter Setsen Khan banners presented horses and camels for the war effort, then donated 2,100 more; Xilingol leagues added 1,200—some accepted, some refused.

sentences.zh: 七年，各部落蒙古王等捐馬六千四百匹，詔納之。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, Mongol princes of the various tribes donated 6,400 horses; an edict accepted them.
translations.idiomatic: Year 7 brought 6,400 horses from Mongol princes of various tribes; the court accepted them.

sentences.zh: 時粵、捻擾畿東，利於用騎也。

translations.literal: At that time the Cantonese and Nian rebels disturbed the capital region, and cavalry was advantageous.
translations.idiomatic: With Cantonese and Nian rebels troubling the capital region, mounted forces had become essential.

sentences.zh: 同治間，黑龍江將軍德英於呼倫貝爾各城勸捐軍馬。

translations.literal: During Tongzhi, Heilongjiang General De Ying urged donation of army horses in the various cities of Hulunbuir.
translations.idiomatic: Under Tongzhi, Heilongjiang General De Ying promoted military horse donations across Hulunbuir's cities.

sentences.zh: 光緒初，豐紳托克湍辦海防，時昭烏達盟郡王捐馬六百匹，因請踵行推廣勸諭，以助軍實雲。

translations.literal: Early in Guangxu, Fengshentuoketuan handled coastal defense; then the prince of Zhaowuda League donated 600 horses, and requested to follow with widespread exhortation to aid military strength.
translations.idiomatic: Early Guangxu, while Fengshentuoketuan managed coastal defense, Zhaowuda League's prince donated 600 horses and urged wider solicitation to bolster the armies.

sentences.zh: 驛置肇自前漢，歷代因之。

translations.literal: Courier stations began in the Former Han and were continued through successive dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: Courier stations date to the Former Han and continued through every dynasty.

sentences.zh: 清沿明制，設驛馬，為額四萬三千三百有奇。

translations.literal: The Qing followed the Ming system and established relay horses, with a quota of somewhat more than 43,300.
translations.idiomatic: The Qing retained the Ming relay-horse system with a quota of just over 43,300 head.

sentences.zh: 各省驛制，定於康熙二年，凡齎奏官驛馬之數，各籓馬五匹，公、將軍、提督、督、撫三匹，總兵、巡鹽御史二匹，從兵部侍郎石麟請也。

translations.literal: Each province's relay regulations were fixed in the second year of Kangxi: for officials bearing memorials, relay horses—each fief, five; dukes, generals, provincial commanders-in-chief, governors-general, and governors, three; brigadier generals and salt censors, two—following Vice Minister of War Shi Lin's request.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial relay rules were set in Kangxi 2: memorial-bearing officials received five horses per fief, three for dukes through governors, two for brigadiers and salt censors—on Vice Minister Shi Lin's petition.

sentences.zh: 邊外之驛，定於九年，凡明詔特遣，及理籓院飭赴蒙古諸部宣諭公務，得乘邊外驛馬。

translations.literal: Frontier relays were fixed in the ninth year: for clear edicts specially dispatched and Board of Mongol Affairs orders to proclaim affairs in the Mongol banners, one might ride frontier relay horses.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier relays were fixed in year 9 for imperial envoys and Board of Mongol Affairs missions to Mongol banners.

sentences.zh: 三十五年，征噶爾丹，設邊外五處驛站，用便車糧運輸。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fifth year, campaigning against Galdan, five frontier relay stations were set up to facilitate grain transport by cart.
translations.idiomatic: Year 35's Galdan campaign established five frontier relay stations to ease cart transport of grain.

sentences.zh: 又從理籓院言，自張家口外設蒙古驛。

translations.literal: Again following the Board of Mongol Affairs, Mongol relays were set from beyond Zhangjiakou.
translations.idiomatic: The Board of Mongol Affairs also established Mongol relays beyond Zhangjiakou.

sentences.zh: 其大略也。

translations.literal: This was the general outline.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the general arrangement.

sentences.zh: 驛傳在僻地者，僅供本州縣所需，亦曰遞馬，額不過數匹。

translations.literal: Relay posts in remote places supplied only what the local prefecture and county needed; also called relay horses, the quota not exceeding a few head.
translations.idiomatic: Remote relay posts served only local county needs as "relay horses," with quotas of just a few head.

sentences.zh: 沖繁州縣，置驛或二或三，額馬至六七十匹。

translations.literal: Busy prefectures and counties set two or three relay stations, with relay horses reaching sixty or seventy.
translations.idiomatic: Busy counties maintained two or three stations with quotas up to sixty or seventy horses.

sentences.zh: 驛差大者，皇華使臣，朝貢蕃客，餘如大臣入覲、蒞官、視鹺、監稅皆是。

translations.literal: Large relay missions: imperial envoys, tribute guests from the frontier, and also such as grand ministers entering audience, taking office, inspecting salt, and supervising taxes.
translations.idiomatic: Major relay duties included imperial envoys, frontier tribute missions, ministers attending court, taking office, salt inspection, and tax supervision.

sentences.zh: 若齎奏員役，呈奉表冊，其小者也。

translations.literal: Such as memorial-bearing clerks presenting tables and registers—these were small.
translations.idiomatic: Memorial clerks bearing registers ranked among the minor duties.

sentences.zh: 要者，如星馳飛遞，刻期立赴之屬。

translations.literal: Important ones were like star-rush flying dispatch, required to arrive by a set deadline.
translations.idiomatic: Urgent cases—star-rush dispatches with fixed deadlines—ranked as important.

sentences.zh: 若閔勞恤死，允給郵傳，其散者也。

translations.literal: Such as condolence and care for the dead, permitted relay service—these were miscellaneous.
translations.idiomatic: Condolence missions granted relay service were classed as miscellaneous.

sentences.zh: 驛政弊壞，張汧嘗極言之。

translations.literal: Relay administration was corrupt and broken; Zhang Qian once spoke of this at length.
translations.idiomatic: Relay administration had rotted; Zhang Qian once denounced it at length.

sentences.zh: 越數誅求，橫索滋擾，蠹國病民，勢所必至。

translations.literal: Repeated exactions beyond number, wanton demands increasingly disturbing—harming the state and injuring the people was inevitable.
translations.idiomatic: Endless extra levies and rampant extortion were bound to drain the treasury and burden the people.

sentences.zh: 已定例諸驛額馬，每年十踣其三，循例買補。

translations.literal: For relay horses at fixed-quota stations, every year three in ten died; replacements were bought by regulation.
translations.idiomatic: Regulation required replacing three relay horses in ten annually at fixed-quota stations.

sentences.zh: 咸豐中，粵氛孔熾，湖、湘境為賊據，劫失驛騎，焚毀號舍，往往有之。

translations.literal: During Xianfeng, Cantonese troubles burned fiercely; Hunan and Hubei territory was held by rebels; relay mounts were robbed and station buildings burned—this often happened.
translations.idiomatic: Xianfeng's raging rebellions seized Hunan and Hubei, repeatedly looting relay horses and burning station houses.

sentences.zh: 各州縣或買馬填補，或賃馬應差，其有失驛未設，即雇夫代馬。

translations.literal: Each prefecture and county either bought horses to fill the gap or hired horses for duty; where a station was lost and not re-established, laborers were hired in place of horses.
translations.idiomatic: Counties bought or hired horses to fill gaps; where stations vanished, hired carriers substituted for mounts.

sentences.zh: 甘肅舊設馬額六千餘，亦以軍興廢弛。

translations.literal: Gansu's old horse quota exceeded 6,000; it too lapsed with the warfare.
translations.idiomatic: Gansu's former quota of 6,000-odd horses likewise collapsed amid warfare.

sentences.zh: 光緒九年，軍務既平，驛遞漸簡，所留馬視前減三分二，而驛政亦無所妨。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Guangxu, after military affairs were settled, relay service gradually simplified; horses retained were reduced by two-thirds from before, yet relay administration was unimpeded.
translations.idiomatic: Guangxu 9, with warfare ended, simplified relays to two-thirds former horse levels without disrupting service.

sentences.zh: 十一年，新疆南路設驛。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, relays were set on Xinjiang's southern route.
translations.idiomatic: Year 11 established relays on Xinjiang's southern route.

sentences.zh: 是時，綜通國驛站歲費，約三百萬餘金。

translations.literal: At that time, totaling relay stations' yearly expense nationwide, it was about three million-odd in cash.
translations.idiomatic: Nationwide relay expenses then ran to about three million taels yearly.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，劉坤一、張之洞條陳新法，謂驛站耗財，不如仿外人之郵政。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year, Liu Kunyi and Zhang Zhidong memorialized on new methods, saying relay stations wasted funds and it would be better to imitate foreigners' postal service.
translations.idiomatic: Year 29, Liu Kunyi and Zhang Zhidong urged reform, arguing relay stations wasted money and foreign-style post would serve better.

sentences.zh: 郵政遞信速，驛政文報遲。

translations.literal: Postal service delivered letters swiftly; relay administration's document reports were slow.
translations.idiomatic: Postal mail moved quickly; relay document runs lagged.

sentences.zh: 弊由有驛州縣馬缺額，又復疲瘦，驛丁或倚為利藪，因致稽延。

translations.literal: The abuse came from relay counties' horses short of quota and again worn thin; relay hands sometimes relied on this as a profit source, thus causing delay.
translations.idiomatic: Abuses stemmed from under-quota, emaciated relay horses and relay hands who profited from delays.

sentences.zh: 請設驛政局，推行郵政，俾驛鋪經費專取給郵資，即三百萬歲耗可以省出矣。

translations.literal: They requested establishing a Relay Administration Bureau, promoting postal service, so relay post expenses would be supplied solely from postal fees—then the three million yearly waste could be saved.
translations.idiomatic: They proposed a Relay Administration Bureau and postal expansion, funding relay costs from postage and saving the three-million-tael annual drain.

sentences.zh: 時韙其言。

translations.literal: At the time his words were approved.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved the proposal.

sentences.zh: 已而驛馬漸裁，嗣是驛遂廢不用。

translations.literal: Soon relay horses were gradually cut; thereafter relays were abandoned and not used.
translations.idiomatic: Relay horses were gradually cut until the system fell into disuse.

sentences.zh: 順治初，建常盈庫，凡車駕司朋椿站銀，武庫司馬值，太僕寺馬價皆儲之。

translations.literal: Early in Shunzhi, the Ever-Full Treasury was built; all the Imperial Carriage Office's compensation silver for relay stations, the Armory's horse values, and the Court of the Imperial Stud's horse prices were stored there.
translations.idiomatic: Early Shunzhi built the Ever-Full Treasury for Imperial Carriage Office relay compensation, Armory horse values, and Court of the Imperial Stud horse prices.

sentences.zh: 康熙初，改常盈庫儲歸戶部。

translations.literal: Early in Kangxi, Ever-Full Treasury stores were transferred to the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Early Kangxi transferred Ever-Full Treasury holdings to the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 乾隆十六年，敕雲南營馬除十踣其三按例應賠外，其逾額踣斃者免賠椿銀。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year of Qianlong, an edict: for Yunnan garrison horses, besides three in ten dying yearly compensated by regulation, those beyond quota that died were exempt from compensation silver.
translations.idiomatic: Qianlong 16 exempted Yunnan garrison horses beyond the regulated three-in-ten annual deaths from compensation silver.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，定給留圈馬乾，每匹視綠營稍優異。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year, fodder allowance for corralled horses was fixed, each head slightly better than Green Standard troops.
translations.idiomatic: Year 27 set corral-horse fodder allowances slightly above Green Standard rates.

sentences.zh: 三十八年，又令雲南買補馬價，每匹減銀三兩。

translations.literal: In the thirty-eighth year, Yunnan's replacement horse price was again ordered reduced by three taels of silver per head.
translations.idiomatic: Year 38 cut Yunnan's replacement horse price by three taels per head.

sentences.zh: 初馬乾歲費約四十四萬有奇。

translations.literal: Initially yearly fodder expense was about 440,000-odd.
translations.idiomatic: Annual fodder costs initially ran to about 440,000 taels.

sentences.zh: 道光中，從載銓等言，裁八旗官拴馬半額，以節出之費補兵餉焉。

translations.literal: During Daoguang, following Zai Quan and others, Eight Banner officials' tethered horses were cut by half the quota, using the saved expense to supplement soldiers' pay.
translations.idiomatic: Daoguang, on Zai Quan and others' advice, halved Eight Banner officers' tethered-horse quotas and redirected savings to troop pay.

sentences.zh: 清初定現任官得養馬，餘悉禁之。

translations.literal: Early in the Qing it was fixed that incumbent officials might keep horses; all others were forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: Early Qing allowed only incumbent officials to keep horses; all others were forbidden.

sentences.zh: 尋許武進士、武舉、兵丁、捕役養馬。

translations.literal: Soon military licentiates, military bachelors, soldiers, and constables were permitted to keep horses.
translations.idiomatic: Soon military licentiates, military bachelors, soldiers, and constables were also permitted.

sentences.zh: 康熙元年，禁民人養馬。

translations.literal: In the first year of Kangxi, common people keeping horses was forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: Kangxi 1 forbade commoners from keeping horses.

sentences.zh: 有私販馬匹，為人首告者，馬給首告之人。

translations.literal: If there was private trafficking in horses and someone informed, the horses were given to the informer.
translations.idiomatic: Private horse trafficking reported to authorities forfeited the animals to the informer.

sentences.zh: 其主有官職，予重罰。

translations.literal: If the owner held office, a heavy penalty was imposed.
translations.idiomatic: Official owners faced heavy penalties.

sentences.zh: 平民荷校鞭責。

translations.literal: Commoners wore the cangue and were flogged.
translations.idiomatic: Commoners wore the cangue and received flogging.

sentences.zh: 十年，令民人仍得養馬。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, common people were again permitted to keep horses.
translations.idiomatic: Year 10 again permitted commoners to keep horses.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，定出廠馬、駝，或踐食田禾，或縱逸侵擾，兵鞭責，官罰俸有差。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year, it was fixed that pasture horses and camels leaving the farm, whether trampling crops or running loose to disturb, soldiers were flogged and officials fined salary by degree.
translations.idiomatic: Year 26 penalized pasture horses or camels that trampled crops or ran loose—soldiers flogged, officials fined by rank.

sentences.zh: 其兵丁強人代牧，乃勒索擾累者，兵發刑部，官降調。

translations.literal: Where soldiers forced others to herd in their place and extorted and harassed, soldiers were sent to the Ministry of Justice and officials demoted or transferred.
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers who forced others to herd for them and extorted payment went to the Ministry of Justice; their officers were demoted.

sentences.zh: 凡牧馬斃，則驗其皮，踣斃例須賠抵，有一九、一七之罰。

translations.literal: Whenever pasture horses died, the hide was inspected; death by falling had to be compensated by regulation, with penalties of one-ninth and one-seventh.
translations.idiomatic: Dead pasture horses required hide inspection; fall-deaths triggered regulated compensation at one-ninth or one-seventh rates.

sentences.zh: 應取駒千匹者，以百匹為一分，百匹者以十匹為一分。

translations.literal: Where 1,000 colts were due, 100 formed one share; where 100, ten formed one share.
translations.idiomatic: Herds owing 1,000 colts counted in shares of 100; herds owing 100 counted in shares of ten.

sentences.zh: 雍正十三年，定馬、駝出廠時，毛齒皆有冊，回日覈驗，如疲瘠十不及三，免議，否則兵鞭責，官罰俸有差。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Yongzheng, when horses and camels left the farm, coat and teeth were all registered; on return day they were verified—if thin and weak did not reach three in ten, investigation was waived; otherwise soldiers were flogged and officials fined salary by degree.
translations.idiomatic: Yongzheng 13 required registered coat and teeth when horses and camels left pasture; on return, if fewer than three in ten were emaciated, officials were spared; otherwise soldiers were flogged and officers fined.

sentences.zh: 乾隆初，禁牧丁等盜馬私售，及與人乘，峻其科罰。

translations.literal: Early in Qianlong, pasture hands and the like stealing horses for private sale and letting others ride were forbidden, with severe penalties.
translations.idiomatic: Early Qianlong forbade pasture hands from stealing horses for private sale or lending mounts, with severe penalties.

sentences.zh: 十六年，嚴牧馬減克料草之罪。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year, the crime of pasture horses having fodder and forage reduced and withheld was strictly enforced.
translations.idiomatic: Year 16 strictly punished withholding pasture horses' fodder.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，官馬出青，每百匹准倒十匹，逾額勒其買補。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year, when government horses went out to green pasture, ten in each hundred might die; beyond the quota they were compelled to buy replacements.
translations.idiomatic: Year 28 allowed ten government horses per hundred to die while out on green pasture; excess deaths required compulsory replacement.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶十一年，行圍木蘭，查獲私販馬匹諸犯，重懲之。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Jiaqing, on the Mulan hunt, persons caught privately trafficking horses were heavily punished.
translations.idiomatic: Jiaqing 11's Mulan hunt brought heavy punishment for private horse traffickers.

sentences.zh: 因諭：「我朝講武時巡，扈從均給官馬。

translations.literal: An instruction followed: "Our dynasty practices martial arts and tours seasonally; the entourage are all given government horses.
translations.idiomatic: An edict followed: "Our dynasty trains in arms and tours seasonally, issuing government horses to the entire entourage.

sentences.zh: 大臣祿入較優，給馬較少。

translations.literal: Grand ministers' salaries are rather ample, so fewer horses are given.
translations.idiomatic: Senior ministers, with ample salaries, receive fewer mounts.

sentences.zh: 官員兵丁，視差務之繁簡，定馬數之多寡，少者一、二匹，多至五匹，事竣原馬還官。

translations.literal: Officials and soldiers, according to the complexity of their duties, fix the number of horses more or less—at minimum one or two, at most five; when the affair ends the original horses return to government.
translations.idiomatic: Officers and soldiers receive one to five horses by duty complexity and return them when the mission ends.

sentences.zh: 如踣斃，呈驗耳尾，仍按價折交。

translations.literal: If they die by falling, ears and tail are presented for inspection and still handed over at converted price.
translations.idiomatic: Fall-deaths require presenting ears and tail for inspection, then paying the converted price.

sentences.zh: 收放時，命王大臣督察。

translations.literal: When receiving and pasturing, princely ministers were ordered to supervise.
translations.idiomatic: Princely ministers were assigned to supervise issue and pasturing.

sentences.zh: 乃官兵等竟私鬻官單，察哈爾官兵收馬利，其折銀易於買補。

translations.literal: Yet officers and soldiers privately sold government chits; Chahar officers and soldiers profited from receiving horses, as the converted silver was easy for buying replacements.
translations.idiomatic: Yet officers sold government chits illegally; Chahar troops profited from receiving horses because conversion silver made replacements easy.

sentences.zh: 積弊日深，大妨馬政。

translations.literal: Abuses deepened daily and greatly obstructed horse administration.
translations.idiomatic: Daily deepening abuses gravely undermined horse administration.

sentences.zh: 自後設有賣單及折收者，一體科罰。

translations.literal: From now on, whoever set up selling chits or converted collection was punished alike.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth selling chits or taking conversion payments alike would be punished.

sentences.zh: 私買之馬販，從嚴問擬。

translations.literal: Private buyers and horse traffickers were to be strictly prosecuted.
translations.idiomatic: Private buyers and horse dealers would face strict prosecution.

sentences.zh: 大臣等其妥議定章以聞。

translations.literal: Grand ministers should properly deliberate and fix regulations to report."
translations.idiomatic: Senior ministers were to draft regulations and report back."

sentences.zh: 」凡營馬或走脫竊失，責令賠補，謂之賠椿，年遞減十之一，至十年悉免之。

translations.literal: Whenever garrison horses escaped or were stolen, compensation was ordered, called compensation for relay; each year reduced by one-tenth, until in ten years all was waived.
translations.idiomatic: Escaped or stolen garrison horses required compensation called peichun, reduced one-tenth yearly until waived after ten years.

sentences.zh: 應敵傷損者免賠。

translations.literal: Those wounded in enemy action were exempt from compensation.
translations.idiomatic: Combat wounds exempted horses from compensation.

sentences.zh: 騎至三年踣斃者亦免。

translations.literal: Those ridden three years and dying by fall were also exempt.
translations.idiomatic: Horses ridden three years and dying by fall were likewise exempt.

sentences.zh: 其餘一年或二三年內踣斃，賠額視其省而異，以十金為最多。

translations.literal: The rest, dying by fall within one or two or three years, compensation quotas differed by province, ten taels at most.
translations.idiomatic: Other fall-deaths within one to three years carried province-varying compensation, capped at ten taels.

sentences.zh: 同治二年，定古北口盤獲私馬逾三十匹者送京，不及三十匹賞與兵丁，著為令。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tongzhi, it was fixed that private horses seized at Gubeikou exceeding thirty head were sent to the capital; fewer than thirty were rewarded to soldiers, established as regulation.
translations.idiomatic: Tongzhi 2 fixed that private horses seized at Gubeikou—over thirty head to the capital, under thirty rewarded to soldiers—as permanent law.
